literal: An unlearned man's natural intelligence, exceedingly good although it be, will not accept those who possess wisdom.
translation: Even if the natural intelligence of an unlearned person is exceedingly great, those who possess true wisdom will not value it.
modern: கல்லாதவனுடைய அறிவு மிகச் சிறந்ததாக இருந்தாலும், அறிவுடையவர்கள் அதனை ஏற்றுக்கொள்ள மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet explains that natural brightness or sharp-wittedness in an unlearned person is not highly valued by the wise. The word 'ஒட்பம்' refers to natural mental sharpness or brilliance. Even if this brilliance appears 'கழிய நன்று' (exceedingly good), those who possess true wisdom ('அறிவுடையார்') will not accept or respect it ('கொள்ளார்'). This is because natural wit, without the discipline and depth of systematic learning, is unstable and lacks real substance.
